messages:
Anya (infra): Heads-up — forecasting shows a sharp winter backlog spike next 6 weeks, small-job mix increases ~2.2x. Packing frag metric climbed in yesterday's sim. Need quick plan on bin-packing adjustments and capacity buys.
Micah: Can you paste the sim output? which policy was used?
Anya (infra): Ran against q4-trace with 'baseline-binpack' and current slice defaults. Quick numbers: cluster utilization falls from 78% -> 61% during the spike; fragmentation score (slots wasted / total slots) 0.19 -> 0.36. GPU-hours demand peak +28%.
Samir: ouch. Did you try lowering min-slot-size or enabling slice-consolidation? those usually recover a chunk.
Anya (infra): Yup — quick A/B: min-slot-size 0.5 -> 0.25 recovers utilization to ~70% but increases 95th latency for small interactive jobs by ~12ms. Also tried soft-reserve pools (10% reserved) — they reduced eviction churn but lowered overall throughput.
Micah: Can you share the sim command + config so I can reproduce?
Anya (infra): Command I used: `./tools/binpack_sim --trace=traces/winter_q4.json --policy=baseline-binpack --min-slot=0.5 --slices=8`
Anya (infra): Config diff I tested:
```
min_slot_size: 0.25    # previously 0.5
eviction_budget_ms: 1200
micro_pool_pct: 10
packing_policy: binpack-stable
```
OpsBot: [alert] region eu-west-1 available GPU capacity < 15% (noticed 19m ago) :rotating_light:
Samir: eu-west is going to be the bottleneck if demand shifts there. Suggest short-term: 1) enable temporary prewarm micro-pools in EU (20 gpus) 2) enable min-slot reduction for burst window 3) raise eviction budget from 1s to 1.5s to avoid thrash.
Marta: cost note: prewarming + reserved burst will add ~12-18% incremental spend on committed months vs current baseline. If we buy extra dedicated capacity for Q4, expect a ~9% discount but 3-6 month commitment.
Leo: Operational playbook idea: canary the min-slot change on a small fleet first (2 racks), monitor 95th latency and eviction rate for 2h, then expand. Who owns the rollout? @Micah? @Samir?
Micah: I can own the canary. Plan: create a canary jobset, enable min-slot-size=0.25 + micro_pool_pct=5, run for 4 hours during low traffic window, measure: cluster_util, packing_frag, eviction_count, 95th latency. If packing_frag improves >10% and eviction_count doesn't spike >15%, promote.
Samir: Also add a fallback that flips back within 15m if 95p latency > threshold. Use the existing rollout API: `/api/v1/rollouts` with policy=threshold-failover.
Anya (infra): I've added the trace outputs and sim artifacts to the infra share: https://redwood.internal/s3/infra/winter_sim/1976543210.tar.gz
Marta: Also thinking longer term: we should evaluate weighted-fairness tweaks that penalize tiny best-effort jobs during seasonal peaks so they don't fragment racks. Could be a config knob exposed in console.
Micah: Agree. Quick change + canary + cost approval gets us through Q4. Samir — can you draft the canary command and rollback playbook?
Samir: On it. Draft will include the CLI we used, metrics to watch, thresholds, and a short runbook for evicting micro-pool if it causes bad tail latency.
Leo: I'll sched a 30m ops sync tomorrow 09:30 to review canary plan and cost trade-offs. Posting calendar invite.
Anya (infra): Thanks all — priority high. Will follow up with a small heatmap of per-tenant fragmentation by region tomorrow.
Micah: Thanks, we'll iterate. :thumbsup:
